questions.stem: Why are food chains usually limited to four or five trophic levels?

options.text: Because there are only a few species in any ecosystem
Because there is not enough energy left to support another trophic level
Because organisms at higher levels grow too large
Because the Sun does not provide enough light

questions.explanation: Energy is lost at each trophic level, so by the fourth or fifth level there is not enough energy remaining to support a viable population of organisms. This limits the length of food chains.
